newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent firmer, supported by higher NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent firmer, supported by higher NYMEX.

text.p: September Brent futures rose on Tuesday, supported by a firmer tone on NYMEX, brokers said.
SIMEX September Brent was last traded at $18.52 per barrel, up 11 cents from London overnight.
NYMEX September crude on the ACCESS system was last traded in Asia at $19.85, for a gain of four cents compared with the New York close at $19.81.

Brokers said the firmer prices were due to a strong gasoline market in the U.S.. The August contract rose 0.81 cent to 64.84 cents per gallon in New York and added 0.66 on ACCESS to last trade at 65.50.
However, gasoline was technically overbought which could undermine crude prices if there was a gasoline sell off, brokers said.
Tom James, Asia-Pacific derivatives manager for Credit Lyonnais Rouse, said gasoline has been leading crude higher, making it susceptible to an about turn.
He said a close in London of the September Brent below $18.47 could be disastrous and could prompt a test of $18 in coming days.
Brokers also said the market was wary of Iraq stepping closer to a resumption of oil exports, which would keep a lid on the upside.
